dcf.method: 5-year FCFF: EBITDA - tax on EBIT - capex - change in net working capital; growth fades linearly from the starting rate to the year-5 rate; Gordon terminal value; equity = EV - borrowings.

reverse_dcf.note: Constant sales growth for five years, at the base margin and the same WACC and terminal growth, that makes the DCF equal today's EV.

blocks.text: [F] Schaeffler India reports on a calendar-year basis (January-December), not the April-March Indian fiscal year; the latest annual report covers 1 January to 31 December 2025 (AR2025 p.9). [AI] This report therefore uses the company's own periods: CY2025 = the year to December 2025, and the latest quarter is April-June 2026, which the company calls Q2 CY26 and which corresponds to Q1 FY27 on an April-March convention. Where our statements data uses column headers such as 'Dec 2025' or 'Jun 2026' these are the same periods (NUMBERS).

[F] Our statements data is consolidated (the listed company plus its wholly owned subsidiary KRSV Innovative Auto Solutions, 'Koovers'), while management's presentations, segment commentary and most annual-report narrative are standalone (NUMBERS; PPT Jul 2026; AR2025 p.176). [AI] Consolidated and standalone figures differ by roughly Rs 290 cr of revenue and Rs 45-50 cr of PAT in CY2025; we flag which basis each figure uses. [F] Earnings-call transcripts are dated by filing month: 'CALL Mar 2026' is the Q4 CY25 call held 25 February 2026, 'CALL May 2026' is the Q1 CY26 call held 30 April 2026, and 'CALL Jul 2026' is the Q2 CY26 call held 23 July 2026 (CALL Mar 2026; CALL May 2026; CALL Jul 2026). [F] The company has been listed for decades (incorporated 27 April 1962; 63rd AGM in 2026), so there is no prospectus or recent-listing issue; no prospectus was available or relevant (AR2025 p.64; AR2025 p.1).

[F] Schaeffler India is the 74.13%-owned Indian subsidiary of Germany's Schaeffler Group, ultimately controlled by INA Holding Schaeffler GmbH & Co. KG (NUMBERS; AR2025 p.110; AR2025 p.134). [F] It makes and sells rolling bearings (ball, roller, needle, spherical, cylindrical, tapered), clutch systems, engine and transmission components, chassis applications, e-mobility systems (e-axle, battery management systems) and aftermarket repair kits (SCREENER; AR2025 p.29-33; CALL Mar 2026). [F] It earns money from four streams: sales to Indian automotive OEMs, sales to industrial OEMs and distributors, the automotive aftermarket, and exports almost entirely to other Schaeffler group companies (AR2025 p.65; CALL May 2026).

[F] Not everything it sells is made in India: in CY2025 standalone sales of manufactured products were Rs 7,315.5 cr and sales of traded products Rs 1,934.3 cr, i.e. about 20.6% of standalone revenue of Rs 9,395.3 cr was resale of goods bought in, largely from group companies (AR2025 p.131; AR2025 p.135) [E]. [F] CIF imports of raw materials, components and products purchased for sale were Rs 3,456.3 cr in CY2025, equal to about 36.8% of standalone revenue [E] (AR2025 p.103).

subsections.title: Bear thesis - the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation leaves no room for error. [F] At Rs 4,008 the stock trades on 50.0x trailing earnings and 32.7x EV/EBITDA; our DCF gives Rs 419 (bear), Rs 736 (base) and Rs 1,005 (bull) per share, and the reverse DCF requires about 70.6% annual sales growth for five years against 10.2% in the base case (NUMBERS).

2. The largest division is barely growing. [F] BIS (39.2% of CY2025 sales) grew 6.5% [E] in CY2025, 4.2% YoY in Q1 CY26 and 5.0% in Q2 CY26 (AR2025 p.142; CALL May 2026; PPT Jul 2026). [MC] Management describes a portfolio 'recalibration' because 'competition is also intensifying' and called automotive bearings 'more commoditized' (CALL May 2026; CALL Jul 2026). [F] An analyst noted a competitor's large SRB/CRB plant beginning operations; management did not dispute it (CALL Mar 2026).

3. Value flows to the parent through related-party channels. [F] In CY2025 the company bought Rs 1,467.5 cr of finished goods and Rs 1,165.6 cr of raw materials and components from group companies (about 28% of standalone revenue [E]), paid technology/trademark fees of Rs 189.0 cr, SAP/IT charges of Rs 79.2 cr and support fees of Rs 110.5 cr (AR2025 p.135). [E] Those three fee lines rose about 39% against revenue growth of 16.3%. [F] Shareholders have approved material related-party transactions of Rs 3,850 cr for 2026, rising 25% a year to 2028 (AR2025 p.99).

4. Export growth is allocated by the group, not won in the market. [MC] 'It is mainly because of intercompany allocations'; 'we don't export directly to the end customers' (CALL Jul 2026; CALL May 2026). [MC] The CFO recalled that exports faltered in 2023 ('We have faced this once in 2023') (CALL Jul 2026). [F] Transfer prices are trued up each December (CALL Jul 2026).

5. Costs are rising faster than they can be recovered. [F] Standalone EBITDA margin was 19.1% in Q2 CY26 vs 19.7% in Q2 CY25 (PPT Jul 2026). [MC] A roughly 10% wage increase and fuel, freight and air-freight costs are 'not subject to the recovery from the customer'; only FX and steel indexation are recoverable (CALL Jul 2026).

6. Cash conversion is weakening again. [F] Standalone working capital rose to Rs 2,029 cr in Q2 CY26 from Rs 1,661 cr in Q4 CY25; H1 CY26 free cash flow was Rs 233.5 cr vs Rs 523.9 cr in H1 CY25 (PPT Jul 2026). [F] CY2025's strong CFO was helped by trade payables rising from Rs 1,128 cr to Rs 1,683 cr, including Rs 853 cr owed to group companies (up from Rs 600 cr) (AR2025 p.149; AR2025 p.130).

7. The Koovers acquisition is loss-making with a distant breakeven. [F] The subsidiary lost Rs 59.5 cr in CY2025 vs Rs 29.5 cr in CY2024, has negative net assets of Rs 95.5 cr, and owes the parent Rs 142 cr of loans (AR2025 p.174; AR2025 p.126). [MC] EBITDA and cash breakeven is now expected in 2029 (CALL Jul 2026).

8. Heavy import and FX exposure. [F] CIF imports were Rs 3,456.3 cr (about 36.8% of standalone revenue [E]); unhedged foreign-currency payables were Rs 402.3 cr at December 2025 (AR2025 p.103; AR2025 p.137). [MC] Q2 CY26 earnings were 'impacted on the foreign exchange effect route' (CALL Jul 2026).

9. Capacity is tight and asset turns are falling. [F] Fixed-asset turnover fell from 6.11x in CY2022 to 4.41x in CY2025 (NUMBERS). [MC] Hosur capacity constraints forced air freight and starved the aftermarket (CALL Jul 2026).
10. Thin float. [F] Promoters hold 74.13%, FIIs 4.36%, DIIs 16.21% and the public 5.29% (Jun 2026) (NUMBERS). [AI] Limited free float amplifies price moves on any disappointment.

Is AT growth share gain or a one-off e-axle ramp? [MC] Management says conventional ICE business grew close to 20% in Q2 and the rest came from e-mobility (CALL Jul 2026). [AI] If e-mobility is a single-platform ramp (an analyst named the Tata Harrier; CALL May 2026), growth could slow sharply once the base annualises. The market may be over-extrapolating 30%+ AT growth.

Is BIS weakness cyclical or competitive? [MC] Management cites Q1 distributor liquidity, wind contract negotiations and railway tender timing (CALL May 2026; CALL Jul 2026). [AI] The admitted pricing pressure and a competitor's new local capacity point to a structural share-of-wallet issue in its highest-quality franchise; the market may be under-weighting this.

Are exports a durable earnings engine? [AI] Bulls see an India-for-the-world hub; bears see a group allocation that can be reversed and priced at arm's length. Both views may be right, which caps how much value the exports deserve.

Is the premium multiple 'owed' to an MNC subsidiary? [AI] The market may be right that low leverage, 26-27% ROCE and parent technology justify a lower discount rate than our 15% WACC. It may also be wrong in assuming related-party economics stay benign.

Does the 2025 cash-flow jump signal a new level? [AI] CFO of Rs 1,290 cr in CY2025 looks like a step-change, but H1 CY26 FCF halved and working capital rose again; the market may be anchoring on a year helped by payables.

blocks.text: [AI] Consensus treats Schaeffler India as a compounding quality franchise riding Indian auto and industrial growth. Our variant view is that the franchise is sound but the growth mix is shifting toward lower-control sources: parent-allocated exports, a single-platform e-mobility ramp and trading of group products. Meanwhile the company's highest-moat business, industrial bearings, is losing momentum to local competition. Earnings quality in CY2025 was flattered by payables, and the fee stack paid to the parent is growing faster than revenue. None of this threatens solvency or the franchise. It does mean that paying 50x trailing earnings, far above every scenario in our DCF model (NUMBERS), assumes an unbroken multi-decade runway that the documents do not evidence.

[AI] The reverse DCF is an artefact of a 15% discount rate and a five-year window. Indian MNC subsidiaries with net cash, high ROCE, parent technology and 30-50% payouts have historically traded at premium multiples because investors discount them at far lower rates and assume growth persisting for decades. On that view, 50x earnings for a business compounding revenue at 12-18% with 26-27% ROCE is expensive but not absurd. The counter-argument does not show the stock is cheap.
